title: Find future bus stop locations in Hamilton, Tennessee
method: Overlay the bus-stop service area (1 polygon, 0-10 min) with three block-group demographic layers (278 block groups): population density, households below poverty (households_ACSHHBPOV) and households without a vehicle (AtRisk_ACSOVEH0), each drawn with its own semi-transparent colour ramp; the service area is outlined on top. Because the supplied density rating is constant, density is derived as total population / land area (persons per km2) in a metric CRS (UTM 16N). The reference also intersects block groups with the service area (served / unserved parts).

key_parameters.overlay: gpd.overlay intersection/difference with the dissolved service area

benchmark_defects: 'populationToPolygonSizeRating' (described as population density) is constant 2.191 for all 278 block groups, so a literal map of it carries no information; checks do not penalise its literal use (reported only).
households_ACSHHBPOV and AtRisk_ACSOVEH0 are household counts, not rates, although the description calls the first a 'poverty rate'.
POP100 and HU100 are entirely empty.
The published reference script performs no geometric overlay; it plots the block-group columns (including populationToPolygonSizeRating) and draws the service-area outline on top.
checks: required: three distinct drawn polygon layers carry poverty (rho>=0.9), no-vehicle (rho>=0.9) and density (pop/area rho>=0.8, or the literal constant rating column)
required: a BusServiceArea-derived layer is plotted (geometry-preserving chain; not centroids / CRS override) and, when captured, matches the service area (IoU>=0.90)
optional: varying population density derived and drawn
optional: geometric overlay of block groups and service area
